dedupe_keys.name: environmental assessment shell canada limited carmon creek project 2009 environmental impact assessment eia and application for approval

description: This Alberta assessment collection describes Shell’s proposed Carmon Creek expansion, about 40 km northeast of Peace River in Northern Sunrise County. Metadata states an expansion target of 80000 barrels per day using vertical steam-drive thermal recovery with initial cyclic steam stimulation, and an assessment deemed complete in 2011. The 22 descriptors include project and environmental-assessment PDFs and an XLSX table of production-casing completion details. Other described attachments cover fracture tests, source-well groundwater analysis and soil calculations. All components belong to one planned-facility assessment collection. A complete numerical model and its executable inputs are not established, and the proposal is not evidence of current production. A specific simulation use is not assigned without further source evidence. The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue provides descriptive metadata and exact original Alberta distribution identifiers. It labels the collection Open Government Licence - Alberta. Access is through the linked descriptive record; current provider access and actual file downloads are untested. Costs are not stated. No document, workbook, archive or dataset body was fetched, and numerical contents have not been independently checked. Related editions and components are grouped only where the source identifies their relationship. The companion registry package identifies the same 2009 Carmon Creek proposal, 80,000-barrel-per-day capacity, vertical steam-drive process, Peace River location and 2011 EIA completion. Its twelve document descriptors include summary, map, reference terms and review notices. It is grouped with the application package as another project component; the documents are not asserted to be identical.
